findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type
findings.body: Check builds the denial-cache key from namespace, UserUID, action, name, and parent folder, but not IdentityType. Anonymous and renderer identities can both have UID 0, and user/service account UIDs may also overlap or be supplied in different forms. A denial cached for one identity type can therefore be returned for another identity type, skipping its permission lookup and causing incorrect access denials. Include the identity type in the denial cache key.

findings.title: Negative cache key can collide because fields are joined with underscores
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates name and parent with underscores and no escaping. Grafana resource and folder UIDs can contain underscores, so different name/parent pairs can produce the same key, for example name a_b with parent c and name a with parent b_c. A denial cached for one combination can then incorrectly deny another resource. Use an unambiguous encoding, hash, or separator that cannot appear in UIDs.

findings.title: Denial cache is checked before positive permissions and never invalidated
findings.body: The denial cache is consulted before any positive cached or database permissions and is only cleared by TTL. If a check is denied while permissions are being created or replicated, the denial entry remains and blocks subsequent checks even after the permission exists. This can keep a creator from accessing a newly created dashboard or folder for the TTL, which conflicts with the stated goal of the PR. Consider checking positive permissions before the denial cache, deleting denial entries when a fresh check allows, or not negative-caching checks for resources that may be in the process of being created.

findings.title: Unauthorized checks can force repeated database permission queries
findings.body: Check now falls back to getIdentityPermissions whenever the cached permission set does not explicitly allow the requested resource, even if the permission cache was just populated. Sequential checks for many distinct unauthorized resources will each trigger a full database permission query before their negative cache entry is written. This can substantially increase database load and can be amplified by authenticated enumeration. Consider limiting requeries, using cache age, or keeping cached-permission denials for non-existent resources.

findings.title: Error-path test does not actually test an error
findings.body: The test case named should return error if store fails does not set fakeStore.err and the test asserts require.NoError, so it never exercises the error path. Add an expected error flag and make the fake store fail for this case.
